event.title: Generic HIV-Prevention Shot Approved, Offering Hope for Low-Income Countries
event.canonical_title: Generic HIV-Prevention Shot Approved, Offering Hope for Low-Income Countries
event.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved a generic version of lenacapavir, the only twice-a-year shot for HIV prevention. This approval is expected to facilitate the drug's availability at lower costs in 120 low- and middle-income countries, raising hopes for improved access to HIV prevention methods.

timeline.title: New HIV-Prevention Drug Lenacapavir Faces Supply Challenges Despite Approval
timeline.summary: Lenacapavir, a new HIV-prevention drug, has shown promising results but is facing significant supply shortages, particularly in Uganda and other parts of Africa. Recently, US regulators approved a generic version for sale in low-income countries, raising hopes for increased accessibility.
key_facts: Lenacapavir is a new HIV-prevention drug.
There is high demand for lenacapavir, outstripping supply in various regions.
A generic version has been approved for sale in low-income countries.
